title: Four unreleased changesets still describe the deleted api-surface-declarations family, and #18991's stated reason to publish rests on a files[] entry that no longer exists
body:
Path: none | 未发布 changeset 的散文(发版即固化) | 四条 changeset 仍在描述已删除的 api-surface-declarations 家族;#18991 的发布理由已落空
分诊重测与定级:2026-09-20T15:32Z

## What was measured

Read first-hand on `origin/main` at 2026-09-20T14:32Z. PR #19024 landed as `2277d1fcd10` — `revert(spec): take back the declaration-text snapshot, restore the 27 signature hashes` — deleting the whole `packages/spec/api-surface-declarations/` family (17 shards plus its build script) and dropping the entry from `packages/spec`'s `files[]`.

**Four unreleased changesets already on main still describe that family in prose**, and changeset prose is compiled verbatim into `CHANGELOG.md` at the next release:

```
.changeset/17108-element-text-variant-published-nine.md
.changeset/18605-enable-on-install-one-authority.md
.changeset/18991-user-export-slot-is-a-real-optin-grant.md
.changeset/19085-metadata-form-declared-rows.md
```

Controls on that reading: 98 changesets on main name `packages/spec` (lit), a fabricated artefact name matches 0 (dark).

## ⭐ The sharpest one is not a stale mention — it is a stale *justification*

`.changeset/18991-user-export-slot-is-a-real-optin-grant.md:20`:

> **Why this publishes rather than taking `skip-changeset`.** Two entries of this package's `files[]` move. `api-surface-declarations/` ships, and the member docblock sits *inside* the `ResolveApiOptions` interface body, so it is part of t…

⇒ the changeset's stated **reason to publish at all** rests on `api-surface-declarations/` being in `files[]`. Measured on main just now, it is not:

```
files[] = ["dist","json-schema","liveness","prompts","llms.txt","README.md",
           "src/**/*.zod.ts","CHANGELOG.md","api-surface","spec-changes.json"]
```

⚠️ ⛔ This card does **not** claim the publish decision is now wrong — the same sentence names a second reason (the member docblock inside the interface body), and whether that one alone carries it is exactly what needs a read. What is certain is that a shipped CHANGELOG entry would tell a reader the package ships a directory it does not.

## Why it is a card and not a rider

All four arrived on the #19237 fix round's branch **with the merge from main**; none is in that PR's diff. Editing other seats' changesets inside a conflict-resolution round would widen it, and the round declined — correctly. ⇒ recorded here so it survives.

## Carrier

The seat that owns the revert `2277d1fcd10` (PR #19024) — these sentences are its wake. Failing that, whoever compiles the next release's `CHANGELOG.md`, which is the moment they reach a consumer and the last moment they can be fixed cheaply.

⚠️ There is a clock on this: once the release compiles, the prose is in a published CHANGELOG and correcting it means another release note, ⛔ not an edit.
